extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of literary criticism; poets and literary critics learning close-reading/practical criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for close-reading lyric/sonnet poetry, illustrated by reader protocols and teacher commentary; aimed at teaching how to judge technical, formal, and emotional aspects of poems. Emphasises sound, rhythm, imagery, clarity, form, and communicative success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity / Understandability
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the poem's sense (thought/argument) can be made out — e.g., many readers were 'bewildered' or 'baffled' and could not construe the poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the central thought of the poem is essential to its structure the reader must be able to comprehend it; obscurity is only acceptable where incoherence or irrationality is a deliberate part of the poem's effect. Provide paraphrase when necessary; assess how many readers 'get' the sense as a measure of clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm / Metrical Regularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistency and appropriateness of metre: iambic pentameter should scan as such; avoid halting, jog-trot, or jig-jigging rhythms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check scansion (feet per line, dominance of iambs where required). Halting rhythm, frequent departures from expected feet, or token attempts at metre (the 'scansion enthusiast') are faults. Good rhythm can elevate ordinary words; poor metre reduces effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound / Sonority and Musicality
rubrics_metrics.description: The poem's control of sonority, use of alliteration, internal rhyme, double rhyme, crescendos, and general musical movement — e.g. 'sonority in the octet' and 'sweet slipping movement of rhythm'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note devices (alliteration, internal rhyme, double rhyme) and dynamic shaping (crescendo, lowering of voice). Sound should be adapted to meaning; effective sound devices contribute to pleasure and communicative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forcefulness of the Closing Lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Strength and decisiveness of the poem's ending — e.g. 'The last two lines lack the forcefulness so desirable at the close of a sonnet' vs. praise when the ending is 'very good and strong'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sonnet (and many lyrics) requires a satisfying close or turning-point; assess whether the final lines deliver the emotional or intellectual culmination intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural Coherence / Relation Between Parts
rubrics_metrics.description: How well different sections (octet/sestet, first/second parts) relate and move — e.g. invocations out of relation to sextet, expectation that a sonnet should conform to foreordained movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the parts fit in proportion, whether transitions are convincing, and whether the poem's 'movement' fulfils genre expectations (sonnet volta, contrasts between sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diction and Word-Choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness, precision and level of diction: trivial or sloppy words reduce effect; choice of words must be capable of being heightened by rhythm and sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for overuse of monosyllables or 'trivial words' that become exposed without a noble rhythm; avoid cheap-magazine tone and sloppiness in lexis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery / Presence of Pictures
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the poem supplies vivid, appropriate images — e.g. criticism that a poem 'is impressive — but leaves no very clear impression; there are no pictures in it'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the poem creates visual or sensory images where needed; some poems intentionally avoid pictorial detail, but if readers expect pictures the poet must supply them or accept the consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and Avoidance of Hackneyed Metaphor
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of fresh, apt metaphors versus stock, hackneyed, obvious nature-images and conventional antitheses (spring/winter, roses/weeds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect conventional 'catchwords' and worn imagery; hackneyed metaphors produce sentimentality or bathos. Original metaphors that carry suggestion are marks of skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity vs Sentimentality
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticity of emotion — whether feeling is genuine or 'pseudo', sentimental, or merely conventional ('sentimentality recollected in very sentimental tranquillity').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether emotion feels lived and convincing; cheap, easy tears or cant phrases indicate insincerity. Without sincerity 'poetry is an impossibility.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicative Efficiency / Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The poem's success in 'getting there' — i.e., penetrating different minds and communicating the same primary modification of consciousness to diverse readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare readers' responses: a poem that consistently produces the same primary impression is communicatively efficient. Divergence may be instructive but extreme scattering suggests failure to communicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of Poetic Form vs Prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the material justifies verse — e.g. 'could have been written quite, if not more, effectively in prose' or where sound alone is the point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide if the poem's effect depends on verse techniques (rhythm, sound, formal movement); if not, the choice of verse may be questioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitability and consistency of tone (e.g., 'cheap-magazine tone', 'pleasing melancholy', 'effeminate weakling') and whether tone suits subject-matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether tone matches emotional content and audience expectation; mismatches (childish treatment of serious subject) are faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of Stock Responses / Reader Preconceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that readers bring conventional reactions ('stock responses') which may colour judgement and that poems may exploit or challenge these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to how personal associations or conventional motifs affect response; the critic should attempt to distinguish stock reaction from genuine response to the poem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance Between Sense and Sound
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate relation of meaning to sonorous qualities — e.g. some readers prefer sound alone, others insist the sense must give relation between parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether the poem's effect relies primarily on sense or on sound; ensure that where sense is necessary it is not obscured by sound devices, and where sound is primary it achieves its aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of Pace and Dynamic Shaping
rubrics_metrics.description: Managing tempo and dynamic contours (slowing, crescendo, lowering of voice) — e.g., 'the first 5 lines sweep up in increasing intensity... then comes the pause... the whole thing quietens off'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether changes of speed and loudness are controlled to support meaning and feeling; stumbling at the end or ill-managed slow-downs are weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Lists / Catalogues
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the use of lists or catalogues contributes or is 'tedious' (e.g. 'list in lines 6 and 7 is tedious').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists should have cumulative force or sonic/semantic purpose; otherwise they become tedious and weaken the poem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhyme Quality and Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Precision and effect of rhyme — perfectness of rhymes, obtrusive obvious rhymes, or effective double rhymes/internal rhymes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge rhyme quality (imperfect rhymes are faults unless used deliberately) and whether rhyme enhances or distorts sense (when rhyme forces a weak word).

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation / Concision
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of compression: whether condensation aids density or merely obscures ('condensation' sometimes a name for ignorance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conciseness is valuable but not at the cost of intelligibility; compressed thought must still be graspable if it is central to structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness of Scansion and Avoidance of Forced Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the metre reads naturally or whether lines require 'cruel forcing' to make five iambic feet; avoid scansion enthusiasts who force readings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer metrical movement that feels organic in speech; forced accents or unnatural beats indicate technical weakness or inexperience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of Technique and Emotional Intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether technical means (metre, diction, sound) faithfully realise the intended emotional goal (e.g., jaunty rhythm contradicting pretended deep passion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique and intended emotional effect should cohere; mismatch (technique implying levity while content claims depth) undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Symbolism
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of symbolical details (e.g. 'rains' suggesting tears) that legitimately enrich meaning vs symbolism that is 'utterly worthless'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols should be apt and carry suggestive train of associations; gratuitous or unclear symbolism weakens the poem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical Value / Lilt and Swing
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall musical charm and singability of a lyric: 'swing and lilt', internal rhymes, pleasing melancholy, 'singing quality'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether line rhythms, internal rhymes, and cadences make the poem pleasurable to read aloud and support its mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactness and Force of Thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Concision and intensity of idea: whether thought is 'compact and forcible' or diffuse and unconvincing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A compact, forcible thought often correlates with strength of poem; diffuseness or lack of compactness suggests failure of structure or expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epigrammatic or Persuasive Conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of a neat, important concluding line or epigram ('epigrammatic conclusion, of importance').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A memorable closing phrase or epigram can crystallise the poem's meaning and give a satisfying end; judge its appropriateness and effectiveness.
